regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Shared PD-1 monotherapy protocol. Select the exact NCCP indication and treatment setting; dedicated services below distinguish lung, colorectal where available, and the authored melanoma pathways.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Lung cancer only: first-line metastatic NSCLC or adjuvant NSCLC after surgery and platinum chemotherapy
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Pembrolizumab: Pembrolizumab is an antibody that blocks PD-1, a control switch on immune T cells. Cancer cells can use this switch to reduce immune attack. Blocking it can help the immune system recognise and attack cancer. The same increased immune activity can inflame healthy organs, which is why new symptoms need attention even after treatment ends.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Pembrolizumab 200 mg is given as a drip over about 30 minutes on Day 1 every 3 weeks (21 days). The hospital visit is longer because of checks and preparation. After complete surgery and platinum chemotherapy, the adjuvant course lasts up to 12 months. For metastatic cancer, treatment continues while it remains helpful and tolerable; the team may consider stopping after 24 months of sustained response without progression, or continuing when appropriate.
key_points: Minimal emetic risk; no usual routine premedication.
No pembrolizumab dose reduction; apply specific hold/permanent-stop and restart criteria.
Grade 4/recurrent grade3 generic immune rules have specific endocrine exceptions; controlled hypothyroidism need not interrupt treatment.
Creatinine is ×ULN, never ×baseline; hepatitis and nephritis thresholds must not be confused with stable organ impairment recommendations.
Every-3–6-week thyroid checks continue on both infusion schedules.
Shared clinical protocol; new patient suite is lung-only.

Abnormal liver tests or creatinine do not establish immune causality. Record clinician-assessed hepatitis/nephritis before the definitive source hold/stop pathway; unexplained abnormalities remain a clinical-review decision.

KEYNOTE-091 final OS analysis at ESMO 2026 did not demonstrate a statistically significant OS improvement; chemotherapy-subgroup DFS figures are updated and labelled separately from metastatic KEYNOTE-024.

Requested restart needs documented source-specific recovery, required steroid management/taper and consultant confirmation. Table 1 endocrine exceptions remain separate; existing 12-week failure/taper and permanent-stop criteria retain priority.

For pembrolizumab, grade 2 immune myocarditis, encephalitis or Guillain–Barré syndrome requires withholding and urgent specialist assessment; grades 3–4 require permanent discontinuation. EMA Table 1 separately addresses myocarditis–myositis–myasthenia gravis overlap: use the highest individual CTCAE v4.0 grade; hold grade 2 and permanently stop grades 3–4.

Before requested restart, document whether any previous event met permanent-discontinuation criteria; absent history is not a negative history. Current recovery, steroid taper and consultant confirmation cannot override a prior permanent-stop event. The safety of reinitiating pembrolizumab after immune myocarditis is not established. Preserve the specific controlled-endocrine continuation exceptions.

Shared-protocol eligibility audit now includes head-and-neck, adjuvant RCC, urothelial and cervical maintenance selection. These are distinct from the existing lung, colorectal and melanoma patient-service contexts.

limitations: These lung trials used pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks. Trial treatment limits and research scan schedules are not automatic NCCP prescribing rules.

context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.

context_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
context_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
context_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
context_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.

notes: HNSCC: adult first-line metastatic/unresectable recurrent squamous disease considered incurable by local therapies; excludes nasopharyngeal primaries; validated PD-L1 CPS ≥1; ECOG 0–2. Adjuvant RCC: adult clear-cell disease at increased recurrence risk after nephrectomy, with metastatic-lesion resection where applicable; ECOG 0–2; start within12weeks of surgery. The initiation window is not a recurring-cycle limit.

Urothelial: separate post-platinum progression and first-line cisplatin-ineligible pathways. Confirm source-appropriate histology/site and advanced setting. First-line requires validated CPS; NCCP indication table ≥10 conflicts with eligibility >10, so exact10 needs reconciliation. Do not impose this CPS threshold on the post-platinum pathway.

Cervical maintenance: adult persistent/recurrent/metastatic disease, induction chemotherapy completed, validated PD-L1 CPS ≥1 and ECOG 0–2. Do not confuse maintenance monotherapy with its induction combination.
